title: Mobile fallback heuristics and minimized SDK surface (notes)
body:
Context
- Goal: define lightweight mobile SDK surface + heuristics for graceful degradation when streaming/tool-calls are impaired (poor network, app backgrounding, intermittent connectivity). Focus is on reducing integration friction for mobile apps that use hosted streaming + tool-calls + structured outputs.

Motivation
- Mobile network conditions vary widely (3G, congested LTE, spotty wifi). Users expect fast interactive feel even when full stream isn't available.
- Current hosted SDKs assume persistent socket+stream and richer client logic; that adds integration work and edge-case behavior (reconnect storms, duplicate tool invocation).
- We need a minimal set of guarantees and small surface that apps can implement quickly, plus server-side fallbacks.

High-level approach
- Offer an "incremental-response" mode optimized for mobile: server returns compact micro-summaries + action frames when streaming is disrupted.
- SDK provides three primitives only: startSession(), onDelta(cb), finalize() — everything else handled by server policies and a tiny helper lib.
- Tool-calls are protected by idempotency tokens + canonical replay token (small opaque string used for dedupe/continued resolution).
- When full streaming fails, server emits a progressive compact snapshot containing: latest content fragment, list of pending tool-calls with statuses, and a resumeToken.

SDK surface (minimal)
- startSession(params: {model, sessionHints, preferStreaming: boolean, bandwidthHint: low|med|high}) -> sessionId
- onDelta(callback(deltaFrame)) -> register handler for incremental content, tool call begin/end, structured output frames, and errors
- finalize(sessionId, mode: close|background|pause) -> returns final snapshot OR resumeToken (if paused)

Delta frame shape (client-visible concept, server sends frames over stream or via final snapshot)
- deltaType: text | microSummary | toolEvent | schemaPatch | error | heartbeat
- content: compact text string (for microSummary/text)
- toolEvent: {toolId, callId, status, resultSummary} (stringified to keep SDK unopinionated)
- schemaPatch: small JSON-schema diff (string)
- resumeToken: included when server wants client to be able to resume later

Server heuristics (fallback rules)
- Bandwidth detection: server maintains RTT + uplink/downlink throughput estimates per session. When throughput < threshold for > N tokens, switch to microSummary mode.
- Background hints: client may call finalize(..., background) to ask server to compress session to resumeToken + pending tool queue.
- Tool-call hedging: for mobile prefer speculative local emulation (client-side stub) AND server-side delayed enforce; use idempotency to prevent double-effect.
- Retry policy: server will retry low-risk tool calls automatically once if a soft failure occurs; client receives toolEvent status -> retried.

Structured output and schema concerns
- Provide compact schema-first frames: server emits minimal schemaIDs + compact value frames rather than full JSON in streaming fallback. Aim to reduce bytes and parsing cost.
- SDK exposes a simple applySchema(schemaId, frames[]) helper that does best-effort reconstruction. Full validation optional, expensive.

Resume semantics and tokens
- resumeToken is small (<= 256 bytes) opaque string that encodes: last stable token index, pending tool call list, server-side KV pointers for cached KV-cache, and a replay nonce.
- Security: resumeToken is signed + time-limited by default (TTL 24h) — product options to extend for dedicated/private customers.
- Replay flow: client calls startSession({resumeToken}) and server reconciles; server emits delta frames starting from last stable point.

SDK ergonomics notes (developer friction)
- Keep public surface tiny (3 methods). Provide separate helper modules for: offline-queue, compact-deserializers, tool-call-stubs.
- Provide default mobile configs: low-power (aggressive microSummary), balanced, fidelity-first. Apps can pass bandwidthHint.
- Avoid forcing app developers to handle resume tokens complexity; default SDK behavior should: auto-store token in secure storage and rehydrate on restart.

Observability / telemetry
- Telemetry events to emit: session_start, fallback_trigger(bandwidth|timeout|background), resume_attempt, tool_call_retry, session_finalize. Low-cardinality props: mobileNetworkType, region, sdkVersion, sessionFidelity.
- Add a sample server-side metric: fallback_rate_by_platform (iOS/Android), median_resume_latency, tool_retry_rate.

Acceptance criteria for MVP
- SDK surface implemented with unit tests and a small sample app (iOS + Android) demonstrating: normal streaming, fallback snapshot, resume, and tool-call life-cycle.
- Server supports resumeToken generation/validation and compact snapshot endpoint.
- Tool-call idempotency works end-to-end (no duplicate side effects in tests).
- Telemetry events appear in console for quick filtering (fallback_rate).

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How opinionated should SDK be about storing resumeToken? Secure store vs. ephemeral memory. Default should be secure but documented.
- TTL defaults for resumeToken — 24h seems reasonable, but enterprise customers may need longer retention. Expose config.
- Do we expose a higher-level "actions API" for common tool types (search, calendar) in SDK or keep it generic? Early preference: keep minimal, provide reference adaptors.
- UX for partially-applied structured outputs: offer a patch-based display or simplified micro-summary? Mobile UIs prefer micro-summary + quick action buttons.

Implementation plan (rough)
- Week 0–2: Proto SDK wrapper + server compact snapshot endpoint + resumeToken format draft.
- Week 3–5: Integration tests with idempotent tool-call flow + sample RN app.
- Week 6: Telemetry and initial console filters, docs draft.
- Week 7–8: Internal playtest with two partner apps; iterate.

Notes to self / TODOs
- Wire up linked artifacts: CONFLUENCE-1234 (detailed session model), GITHUB-PR-7890 (server resume prototype), JIRA-API-452 (tool idempotency infra).
- Draft sample UX flows for low-bandwidth: show micro-summary + "continue full response" button that triggers resume.
- Decide on default bandwidthHint mapping for Android network types.

Risks
- Server complexity: maintaining snapshot/resume for many short-lived mobile sessions could add state pressure. Mitigation: make snapshots ephemeral and store only pointers for dedicated/private customers when needed.
- Developer confusion: too many heuristics hidden in SDK -> add clear docs and visible telemetry.

Short term experiments to validate
- A/B test with 2 partner apps: (A) current streaming always vs (B) streaming + microSummary fallback. Measure perceived latency, completion rate, and user retry clicks.
- Synthetic network lab: run sessions through 3G/limited-512kbps and verify bytes saved and resume success rate.

End"
